subject.title: [Bug]: Codex app-server session wedges indefinitely after a 429 rate-limit burst — terminal-idle watchdog still gated by `activeAppServerTurnRequests > 0` (regression/incomplete fix of #82681)

question: Should this issue close now based on current-main source proof from the run-lifecycle stack, or stay open until a release containing that stack has live 429-burst confirmation?
rationale: The source and tests strongly suggest the reported 429-silent path no longer wedges indefinitely, but the latest human comment explicitly keeps the issue open pending live confirmation and the literal terminal-idle gate request was intentionally rejected.

options.title: Wait For Release Live Proof
options.body: Keep this issue open until a build containing the run-lifecycle stack is tested against the 429-burst scenario or equivalent redacted traces show bounded recovery.

options.title: Close As Main-Only Fixed
options.body: Close this issue as implemented on current main using the merged run-lifecycle stack as sufficient structural proof, while asking for a fresh issue if 429 traces still wedge.

options.title: Split Remaining Gate Concern
options.body: Close the 429 wedge only if a narrower follow-up tracks stuck server-to-client request handlers that can keep activeAppServerTurnRequests positive.

recommendation.title: Wait For Release Live Proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a build containing the run-lifecycle stack is tested against the 429-burst scenario or equivalent redacted traces show bounded recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the status comment and merged the run-lifecycle stack that currently owns the decision boundary.
